question.text:
Which of the following pairs $(x,y)$ are solutions of the Diophantine equation $5x+2y=75?$

  1. $(11,10)$
  2. $(10,15)$
  3. $(5,25)$
question.explanation:
Let's check each pair in turn.

  • $(11,10)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=11$ and $y=10,$ we obtain \begin{align*} 5x+2y &= 75 \\[3pt] 5 \cdot 11+2 \cdot 10 &= 75 \\[3pt] 55+20 &= 75 \\[3pt] 75 &= 75 \quad {\color{green}\checkmark} \end{align*}

  • $(10,15)$ is not a solution of our equation. Substituting $x=10$ and $y=15,$ we obtain \begin{align*} 5x+2y &= 75 \\[3pt] 5 \cdot 10 + 2 \cdot 15 &= 75 \\[3pt] 50+30 &= 75 \\[3pt] 80 &\neq 75 \quad {\color{red}\times} \end{align*}

  • $(5,25)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=5$ and $y=25,$ we obtain \begin{align*} 5x+2y &= 75 \\[3pt] 5 \cdot 5 + 2 \cdot 25 &= 75 \\[3pt] 25+50 &= 75 \\[3pt] 75 &= 75 \quad {\color{green}\checkmark} \end{align*}

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

  • $(5,22)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=5$ and $y=22,$ we obtain \begin{align*} 9x-2y &= 1 \\[3pt] 9 \cdot 5 - 2 \cdot 22 &= 1 \\[3pt] 45-44 &= 1 \\[3pt] 1 &= 1 \quad {\color{green}\checkmark} \end{align*}

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

question.text:
Which of the following Diophantine equations have solutions?

  1. $4x+12y=6$
  2. $2x+12y=4$
  3. $-3x+5y=2$
question.explanation:
Recall that a linear Diophantine equation \[ ax+by=c \] has a solution if and only if $d \: | \: c,$ where $d = \text{gcd}(a,b).$

With that in mind, let's examine each equation in turn.

  • Equation I has no solution. We have $a=4,$ $b=12,$ and $c=6.$ Since \[ d=\text{gcd}(4,12)=4 \] and $4 \!\not{|}\: 6,$ our equation has no solution.

  • Equation II has solutions. We have $a=2,$ $b=12,$ and $c=4.$ Since \[ d=\text{gcd}(2,12)=2 \] and $2 \: | \: 4,$ our equation has solutions.

  • Equation III has solutions. We have $a=-3,$ $b=5,$ and $c=2.$ Since \[ d=\text{gcd}(-3,5)=1 \] and $1 \: | \: 2,$ our equation has solutions.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the General Solution of a Linear Diophantine Equation Given One of Its Solutions

question.text: Given that $(x,y)=(1,-2)$ is a solution of the Diophantine equation $3x+6y=-9,$ and that $(\overset{\sim}{x},\overset{\sim}{y})$ is the solution with the smallest possible positive value of $x,$ what is the value of $\overset{\sim}{x}?$
question.explanation:
First, recall that a linear Diophantine equation \[ ax+by=c \] has a solution if and only if $d \: | \: c,$ where $d = \text{gcd}(a,b).$ Moreover, if $(x_0,y_0)$ is a solution to the equation, then the general solution is given by \[ \left(x_0+\dfrac{b}{d}t, \, y_0-\dfrac{a}{d}t\right), \qquad t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \]

Here, we have $a=3,$ $b=6,$ $c=-9,$ and \[ d=\text{gcd}(3,6)=3. \]

Since $(1,-2)$ is a solution of $3x+6y=-9,$ the general solution must be

\[ \left(1+\dfrac{6}{3}t, \, -2-\dfrac{3}{3}t\right) = (1+2t, \, -2-t), \]

where $t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \, .$

The smallest possible positive value of $x=1+2t$ is attained when $t=0.$ Therefore,

\[ \overset{\sim}{x} = 1+2 \cdot 0 = 1. \]

question.text: Given that $(x,y)=(-4,-7)$ is a solution of the Diophantine equation $7x-3y=-7,$ and that $(\overset{\sim}{x},\overset{\sim}{y})$ is the solution with the greatest possible negative value of $y,$ what is the value of $\overset{\sim}{y}?$
question.explanation:
First, recall that a linear Diophantine equation \[ ax+by=c \] has a solution if and only if $d \: | \: c,$ where $d = \text{gcd}(a,b).$ Moreover, if $(x_0,y_0)$ is a solution to the equation, then the general solution is given by \[ \left(x_0+\dfrac{b}{d}t, \, y_0-\dfrac{a}{d}t\right), \qquad t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \]

Here, we have $a=7,$ $b=-3,$ $c=-7,$ and \[ d=\text{gcd}(7,-3)=1. \]

Since $(-4,-7)$ is a solution of $7x-3y=-7,$ the general solution must be

\[ \left(-4+\dfrac{(-3)}{1}t, \, -7-\dfrac{7}{1}t\right) = (-4-3t, \, -7-7t), \]

where $t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \, .$

The greatest possible negative value of $y=-7-7t$ is attained when $t=0.$ Therefore,

\[ \overset{\sim}{y} = -7-7 \cdot 0 = -7. \]

question.text: Consider the Diophantine equation $4x+7y=9.$ The integer pair $(\overset{\sim}{x},\overset{\sim}{y})$ is the solution with the smallest possible positive value of $x.$ What is the value of $\overset{\sim}{x}?$
question.explanation:
We have the linear Diophantine equation

\[ ax+by=c \] where $a=4,$ $b=7,$ and $c=9.$ We're given that the equation has solutions.

Notice that our equation can't be solved for either of the two variables using integer coefficients. So, let's find the linear representation of $\text{gcd}(7,4)$ using the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} 7 & = & 4 \cdot 1 & + & 3 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 4 & = & 3\cdot 1 & + & 1 \end{matrix} \end{align*}

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} 3 &= 7 - 4 \cdot 1 \\[3pt] 1 &= 4 - 3. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 1 &= 4-3 \\[3pt] &= 4-(7-4) \\[3pt] &= 4 \cdot 2 + 7 \cdot (-1). \end{align*}

As a result, we obtain that $d=\text{gcd}(a,b) = 1$ and

\[ 4 \cdot 2 + 7 \cdot (-1) = 1. \]

Multiplying this equation by $9,$ we get

\begin{align*} 4 \cdot 2 + 7 \cdot (-1) &= 1 \\[3pt] 4 \cdot 2 \cdot 9 + 7 \cdot (-1) \cdot 9 &= 9 \\[3pt] 4 \cdot 18 + 7 \cdot (-9) &= 9, \end{align*}

which means that $(x,y)=(18,-9)$ is a solution to our Diophantine equation.

Now, the general solution is

\[ \left(18+\dfrac{b}{d}t, \, -9-\dfrac{a}{d}t\right) = (18+7t, \, -9-4t), \]

where $t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \,.$

The smallest possible positive value of $x=18+7t$ is attained when $t=-2.$ Therefore,

\[ \overset{\sim}{x} = 18+7 \cdot (-2) = 4. \]

question.text: Consider the Diophantine equation $9x+11y=6.$ The integer pair $(\overset{\sim}{x},\overset{\sim}{y})$ is the solution with the greatest possible negative value of $y.$ What is the value of $\overset{\sim}{y}?$
question.explanation:
We have the linear Diophantine equation

\[ ax+by=c \] where $a=9,$ $b=11,$ and $c=6.$ We're given that the equation has solutions.

Notice that our equation can't be solved for either of the two variables using integer coefficients. So, let's find the linear representation of $\text{gcd}(9,11)$ using the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} 11 & = & 9 \cdot 1 & + & 2 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 9 & = & 2\cdot 4 & + & 1 \end{matrix} \end{align*}

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} 2 &= 11 - 9 \\[3pt] 1 &= 9 - 2\cdot 4. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 1 &= 9-2\cdot 4 \\[3pt] &= 9-4(11-9) \\[3pt] &= 9 \cdot 5 + 11 \cdot (-4). \end{align*}

As a result, we obtain that $d=\text{gcd}(a,b) = 1$ and

\[ 9 \cdot 5 + 11 \cdot (-4) = 1. \]

Multiplying this equation by $6,$ we get

\begin{align*} 9 \cdot 5 + 11 \cdot (-4) &= 1 \\[3pt] 9 \cdot 5 \cdot 6 + 11 \cdot (-4) \cdot 6 &= 6 \\[3pt] 9 \cdot 30 + 11 \cdot (-24) &= 6, \end{align*}

which means that $(x,y)=(30,-24)$ is a solution to our Diophantine equation.

Now, the general solution is

\[ \left(30+\dfrac{b}{d}t, \, -24-\dfrac{a}{d}t\right) = (30+11t, \, -24-9t), \]

where $t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \,.$

The greatest possible negative value of $y=-24-9t$ is attained when $t=-2.$ Therefore,

\[ \overset{\sim}{y} = -24-9 \cdot (-2) = -6. \]

\[ \overset{\sim}{x} = 28+11 \cdot (-2) = 6. \]

\[ ax+by=c \] where $a=5,$ $b=9,$ and $c=8.$ We're given that the equation has solutions.

Notice that our equation can't be solved for either of the two variables using integer coefficients. So, let's find the linear representation of $\text{gcd}(5,9)$ using the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} 9 & = & 5 \cdot 1 & + & 4 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 5 & = & 4\cdot 1 & + & 1 \end{matrix} \end{align*}

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} 4 &= 9 - 5\cdot 1 \\[3pt] 1 &= 5 - 4. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 1 &= 5-4 \\[3pt] &= 5-(9-5) \\[3pt] &= 5 \cdot 2 + 9 \cdot (-1). \end{align*}

As a result, we obtain that $d=\text{gcd}(a,b) = 1$ and

\[ 5 \cdot 2 + 9 \cdot (-1) = 1. \]

Multiplying this equation by $8,$ we get

\begin{align*} 5 \cdot 2 + 9 \cdot (-1) &= 1 \\[3pt] 5 \cdot 2 \cdot 8 + 9 \cdot (-1) \cdot 8 &= 8 \\[3pt] 5 \cdot 16 + 9 \cdot (-8) &= 8, \end{align*}

which means that $(x,y)=(16,-8)$ is a solution to our Diophantine equation.

Now, the general solution is

\[ \left(16+\dfrac{b}{d}t, \, -8-\dfrac{a}{d}t\right) = (16+9t, \, -8-5t), \]

where $t=0, \pm1, \pm2, \ldots \,.$

The smallest possible positive value of $x=16+9t$ is attained when $t=-1.$ Therefore,

\[ \overset{\sim}{x} = 16+9 \cdot (-1) = 7. \]

example.title: Solving a Linear Diophantine Equation
